record.paper_title: Non-Supersymmetric (but) Extreme Black Holes, Scalar Hair and Other Open Problems
record.original_question: What is the most general black-hole solution of N = 8, d = 4 supergravity, including extremal but non-supersymmetric cases, and do all N = 8 supergravity extreme black-hole solutions satisfy the expected generalized duality-invariant Bogomol'nyi identity M⁻⁶ ∏ᵢ₌₁⁴(M² − |Zᵢ|²) = 0, where the Zᵢ are central-charge eigenvalues?

evidence.quote: where the Zi's are the central charge matrix's complex skew eigenvalues and are complicated combinations of the electric and magnetic charges of the vector fields in the supergravity multiplet (graviphotons) and the constant values of the scalars at infinity (moduli).

The most general solution is unknown. We have already discussed that there are extremal but non-supersymmetric BH solutions in this theory. In any case we expect that all N = 8 SUGRA extreme BH solutions satisfy a generalized duality-invariant B identity of the form M−6 Y 4 i=1 (M2 − |Zi|2) = 0 .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider $\mathcal{N}=8$, $d=4$ supergravity. Its bosonic field content includes the graviton, 28 vector fields (graviphotons), and 70 scalars parametrizing the coset $E_{7(7)}/SU(8)$. For any stationary, asymptotically flat black-hole solution of this theory, the central-charge matrix $Z_{AB}$ (an antisymmetric $8\times 8$ complex matrix built from the electric and magnetic charges of the 28 vectors together with the asymptotic values of the scalar moduli) can be skew-diagonalized to yield four complex skew eigenvalues $Z_1, Z_2, Z_3, Z_4$. Let $M$ denote the ADM mass.

(a) Determine the most general black-hole solution of $\mathcal{N}=8$, $d=4$ supergravity, including the extremal but non-supersymmetric branches.

(b) Prove or disprove that every extreme (extremal) black-hole solution of $\mathcal{N}=8$, $d=4$ supergravity satisfies the generalized duality-invariant Bogomol'nyi-type identity
$$M^{-6}\prod_{i=1}^{4}\bigl(M^{2}-|Z_{i}|^{2}\bigr)=0.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Chow and Compère (arXiv:1404.2602, Phys. Rev. D 90 (2014) 025029) constructed the most general asymptotically flat, stationary, rotating, non-extremal black hole of the STU model and used U-duality to generate the most general such black hole of N=8 supergravity, discussing its extremal limits (supersymmetric and non-supersymmetric) and BPS-type bounds. This addresses part (a) of the question. The precise generalized duality-invariant Bogomol'nyi identity for all extreme N=8 solutions in the exact form stated is consistent with the central-charge structure (eigenvalues equal to M characterizing fractional BPS and non-BPS extremal limits), but a general published proof for all extremal—including non-supersymmetric—branches in that exact factorized form is not clearly identified, so the problem appears partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Black holes in N=8 supergravity from SO(4,4) hidden symmetries
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of the most general asymptotically flat, stationary, rotating, non-extremal, dyonic black hole of the STU model, generating via U-dualities the most general asymptotically flat, stationary black hole of N=8 supergravity.
status_evidence.claim: The most general stationary black hole of N=8, d=4 supergravity has been constructed, addressing part (a).

status_evidence.title: Supersymmetric black holes in N=8 supergravity
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses BPS bounds and central-charge eigenvalues for N=8 black holes.
status_evidence.claim: The structure of central charges and BPS bounds in N=8 supergravity supports the proposed Bogomol'nyi-type identity.
